page: Microsoft Azure E8-2ds_v4 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the EDSv4 family. Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, it features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at 2.6 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 vCPUs. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core density of 32.0 GB per core. For local storage, the instance includes a 307 GB local SSD and supports Premium Storage. No GPUs are present in this configuration.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance profile characterized by average single-threaded capabilities but limited multi-core and memory throughput. The single-core performance is moderate, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1265.0 and average single-threaded compression and decompression speeds, such as 23.86 GB/sec for gzip. However, due to the low core count, multi-core benchmarks are constrained, as evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 1516.0 and a stress-ng multi-core CPU performance of 1846.68. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with large block read-only bandwidth at 13.86 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 11.03 GB/sec. Database operations and web serving throughput are similarly low, with Redis SET operations reaching 1.8 million operations per second and static web serving throughput at 2.02 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers high memory density and local SSD storage relative to its compute resources, making it a specialized option for workloads requiring significant RAM but minimal CPU processing. The presence of 64.0 GB of RAM alongside a 307 GB local SSD makes it suitable for memory-intensive applications, small caching layers, or database workloads that do not require high parallel processing power. It is less suitable for compute-heavy tasks, software compilation, or multi-threaded data processing due to the physical core limitation.

It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8272CL processor with 1 physical core and 2 vCPUs running at 2.6 GHz. The instance is configured with 64.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 32.0 GB per core, and includes a 307 GB local SSD with Premium Storage capability. Benchmark results indicate average single-core performance, such as a Geekbench single-core score of 1265.0, but poor multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics due to the low core count. This hardware profile offers high memory density and local storage capacity relative to compute resources, making it qualitatively cost-effective for memory-heavy, low-compute workloads. It is best suited for small databases, caching layers, and memory-intensive applications that do not require extensive parallel processing.
